subject.title: Codex-OAuth models fail over incorrectly — sibling model with healthy per-model quota still drops to non-codex fallback

question: After the model-scoped auth-profile fix lands, should Codex OAuth sibling fallback stay on the Codex app-server while upstream websocket/rate-limit behavior is investigated, or should OpenClaw add a direct-runtime Codex Harmony tool-call adapter as a supported fallback path?
rationale: The remaining choice changes runtime ownership, provider routing, and tool-call parsing behavior, and the exact app-server 429 mechanism needs maintainer-owned live quota proof before automation can safely pick a direction.

options.title: Finish app-server path first
options.body: Land or replace #99810, keep the Codex app-server as the default runtime, and require live proof of the suspected upstream websocket/rate-limit context bug before changing routing.

options.title: Build direct Harmony support
options.body: Add a bounded direct OpenAI Responses adapter for Codex Harmony tool calls and consider explicit direct-runtime fallback only after real tool-call proof.

options.title: Defer pending stronger trace
options.body: Keep both runtime paths unchanged until a maintainer-owned live trace proves whether the app-server, OpenClaw cooldown state, or both are responsible.

recommendation.title: Finish app-server path first
recommendation.body: Land or replace #99810, keep the Codex app-server as the default runtime, and require live proof of the suspected upstream websocket/rate-limit context bug before changing routing.

likelyOwner.reason: They are already pulled into the issue and have the closest recent provider/runtime history for the routing and adapter decision.
